pages.title: Wave Packet
pages.text: A localised bump made by adding waves of slightly different frequencies so they reinforce in one place and cancel elsewhere. Quantum particles are wave packets, which is why their position and momentum cannot both be sharp. The packet seems to spread slowly the longer you watch it.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Adding up a Fourier series of entangled photon modes in the Analytic Continuator, I built a pulse of light localised in space. Its spread in frequency and position balanced exactly as Heisenberg said.

Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$() and $(item)Neutron Interferometer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): High-Energy Particle Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Quantum Field Lattice, Quantum Singularity.
